CHIEF COMPLAINT
Chest pain that occurred three months ago, referred from the emergency room for evaluation of esophagitis.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a new patient with a referral from the ER. She presented with chest pain in early October 2026 that lasted four days. The pain was located in the center of her chest behind her breastbone and described as sharp, feeling like a heart attack. The pain occurred randomly and nothing she did relieved it. She went to the emergency room after four days due to inability to manage the pain. At that time, an EKG and blood tests were performed, all normal. She denies cardiac etiology was found. Associated symptoms included possible heartburn or indigestion and difficulty swallowing. The pain was worse with eating. Both the chest pain and swallowing difficulty resolved approximately three days after the ER visit. She has been asymptomatic for the past three months since the initial episode. She denies current abdominal pain. She reports being under significant stress from a job transition at the time of symptom onset. She has been attempting to lose weight.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies current chest pain. Denies heartburn prior to this episode, though possibly had some with the acute event. Denies current difficulty swallowing. Denies abdominal pain. Bowel movements are normal.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Uterine fibroids, anemia, cholecystectomy several years ago.

MEDICATIONS
Not discussed.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Denies family history of GI problems.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient reports a stressful job transition that occurred around the time of her chest pain episode in early October 2026.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Abdomen: Soft. Lower abdomen non-tender to palpation. Upper abdominal quadrants with mild tenderness to light palpation, about equal on both left and right. Otherwise, exam appears normal.

RESULTS
ER workup including cardiac workup, EKG, and blood tests were normal.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Differential diagnosis includes GERD, dyspepsia, esophagitis, musculoskeletal etiologies, and anxiety. Assessment that patient likely experienced an anxiety attack related to her job transition, with possible contribution from musculoskeletal etiologies and/or intense heartburn for a few days. Given that symptoms occurred three months ago and have completely resolved, esophagitis if present would likely have healed by now. Discussed EGD (upper endoscopy) versus clinical monitoring. Patient elected to self-monitor her symptoms. She will call the office if she experiences any additional episodes of pain or other concerning symptoms, at which time an EGD can be scheduled. She may follow up as needed for any other GI complaints.
